confidential_wrapper.public_trace_boundary: wrap recipient and deposited USDC amount are public. Subsequent confidential token amounts/balances cannot be reconstructed from public ERC20 flows without authorised decryption or a disclosed accounting statement.

control_state_at_T.meaning: The owner can add decryption observers, set a pauser, block users and authorise upgrades. A zero pauser means no address currently has the pause role. The empty global observer list does not audit wallet-authorised decryption access or remove the owner power to change these settings.

post_wrap_public_boundary.scope: Public cUSDC event census for this wallet from its measured wrap through T, plus public amount disclosures in that wrapper. Ciphertext handles are not plaintext amounts. Receiver-filtered unwraps do not cover unwrapping to other receiver addresses.
post_wrap_public_boundary.interpretation: Public routing shows confidential batch joins and a verified batcher's Quit refund events. Encrypted handles do not establish positive transferred quantities, realised yield, exact allocation of the first wrap, or whole-wallet profit. The later additional wrap and incoming confidential events prevent exclusive attribution of fungible balances.

registry_observations.scope: Existing official V1 repository and lens plus the previously queried current factory generation. Selected ETH assets come from the measured official Compound Arbitrum collateral routes. Not all Silo generations or assets.

findings.title: Vault income did not cover the measured borrowing cost
findings.text: The two borrowed USDC lots receive an allocated 91.840383 USDC of vault income but incur about 239.889887 USDC of funding cost by redemption. Their allocated funded result at that exit is approximately -148.049504 USDC before gas. This is a lot allocation and debt valuation, not a measured repayment or whole-wallet cash profit. The PYUSD sequence receives 1.948867 PYUSD above its deposit. Borrowing cost, including the exact residual liability in the repayment-block state, is 2.347298 PYUSD. Its funded result is -0.398431 PYUSD before gas.

findings.title: The USDC exit enters a verified confidential wrapper
findings.text: The full 1,700,553.396390 USDC redemption is wrapped into Zama cUSDC for the same wallet eight minutes later. Public data establish the amount and recipient at this boundary. They do not reveal a complete subsequent allocation or prove that the loan was repaid.

findings.title: The PYUSD exit leaves debt and collateral
findings.text: The wallet redeems every PYUSD vault share, repays 1,000,001 PYUSD and withdraws 699.994930347918797441 weETH. The repayment-block state retains 1.347298 PYUSD of debt and 0.005069652081202559 weETH. The borrow shares and collateral remain at T, and interest continues.

findings.title: Vault fees are already reflected in the measured cash income
findings.text: The deployed USDC vault has a 10% performance fee and the PYUSD vault has a 15% performance fee at exit and T. Both have a zero management fee in those observations. Standard redemption uses a fee-aware share conversion. The measured income must not be reduced by the headline performance fee a second time.

findings.title: Selected Silo deployments have little measured dollar-token debt
findings.text: Three selected Ethereum V1 ETH-family markets have about 1.79602246 XAI of bridge debt. Two selected Arbitrum V1 ETH-family markets have 212.334440 units of bridged USDC debt. These are entire bridge-asset loan totals in selected Silos, not a verified dollar valuation or a census of all Silo markets. The earlier Arbitrum archive errors are repaired through a public Blast endpoint at the unchanged snapshot block.

findings.title: The repaired Arbitrum factory contains four canonical lending pairs
findings.text: All 13 configurations and 26 silo assets are resolved in the examined Arbitrum factory generation. Four configurations pair canonical WETH with native USDC; together they have 0.088410 USDC of debt with interest at T. This measures a dated generation rather than implying that all Silo deployments are empty or small.

findings.title: The confidential route is visible, but its quantities remain private
findings.text: The complete stated cUSDC wallet queries find two outgoing encrypted-transfer events, eight incoming events and two public wraps through T. The second wrap adds 2,002,038.655059 USDC on 17 September. Receipts show confidential batch Joined events and the verified deposit batcher's Quit events returning encrypted cUSDC. No receiver-wallet UnwrapFinalized event or public AmountDisclosed event is observed in this wrapper and window. These are public routing and refund events, not measured positive confidential quantities or proof of a completed yield investment.

missing_public_inputs: Public confidential-token balances and post-wrap allocation require authorised decryption or a disclosed statement.
The completed cUSDC wallet-filtered event census does not trace every other receiver or reconstruct full-wallet debt and reward history.
Separate cash flows cannot establish exclusive funding by fungible loan proceeds. Pro-rata lot return is a stated analytical allocation.

Destination share income includes deployed vault fees. Other rewards, collateral staking income, wallet assets, gas-to-USD conversion, taxes and any outside fees are not included in whole-wallet profit, which remains unknown.
No beneficial owner is verified for either borrower. A historical lending-to-yield route does not identify the whole wallet or its current carry allocation.
Other Silo factory generations, legacy assets and account-level collateral allocation remain outside the bounded registry and selected market reads.
